title: Olonkho, Yakut Heroic Epic
summary: Olonkho is the heroic epic tradition of the Sakha (Yakut) people, a name for both the whole tradition and its central epic, which UNESCO calls one of the oldest epic arts of the Turkic peoples. Performers called olonkhosuts alternate sung verse with recitative, telling of warriors, deities and spirits. Threatened by twentieth-century change, it was proclaimed a UNESCO Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity on 25 November 2005 and inscribed on the Representative List in 2008, prompting a Sakha state preservation programme.

uncertainty.note: Dates are of the UNESCO proclamation (25 November 2005) and Representative List inscription (2008). The opened sources give no firm date for the origin of the epic tradition; the id year 1000 is only a lookup key.

where.modern_name: Yakutsk, Sakha Republic (Yakutia), Russia (proxy pin for the Sakha Republic)

importance.justification: Central oral epic tradition of the Sakha people, recognised by UNESCO as intangible heritage of humanity.
